criteria.name: Editable CAD
criteria.desc: Design source in a form you could change: native parametric files or a public Onshape document. STL or STEP exports alone count as partial.

criteria.name: Itemised BOM
criteria.desc: Every purchased part with quantity, price and a vendor or part number.

criteria.name: Build documentation
criteria.desc: Assembly instructions or a build guide a third party could follow: print settings, order of assembly, wiring.

criteria.name: Electronics source
criteria.desc: Schematics and PCB files for any custom board, or every board is an off-the-shelf part.

criteria.name: Firmware and low-level code
criteria.desc: The code that talks to the actuators and runs the control loop on the robot.

criteria.name: Robot description and simulation
criteria.desc: URDF, MJCF or USD with masses and limits, and a simulation setup that uses it.

criteria.name: Working controller
criteria.desc: A released controller or trained policy that makes the released hardware stand and walk (or, for arms and hands, move usefully).

criteria.name: Open hardware licence
criteria.desc: A stated hardware licence that permits study, modification, manufacture and sale (OSHWA definition): CERN-OHL, CC BY, CC BY-SA, MIT, Apache, BSD, Solderpad. Non-commercial terms or no licence fail.

criteria.name: Reproduced
criteria.desc: Built by the authors and reproduced by someone else, or sold as a kit; the release has been shown to be buildable.

forms.name: Humanoid
forms.desc: Two legs, a torso and two arms; walks or is meant to.

forms.name: Bimanual
forms.desc: Two arms on a fixed torso or stand.

forms.name: Bimanual + mobile
forms.desc: Two arms on a wheeled base.

forms.name: Mobile manipulator
forms.desc: One arm on a wheeled base.

slots.name: Lower body
slots.desc: Pelvis, hips, legs and feet, with their actuators.

slots.name: Torso
slots.desc: Waist joint, frame, computer, power and IMU.

robstride-rs.name: RobStride RS-series
robstride-rs.protocol: RobStride private CAN protocol, MIT-mode PD

odri.name: ODRI brushless module
odri.bus: SPI to master board, Ethernet to PC

robots.name: Fully Open Humanoid v0.2
robots.structure: FDM-printed PETG-CF and PLA, four 2020 extrusions
robots.price_note: Core BOM, priced 2026-09; unbuilt design.

open_notes.cad: Generated from tools/build_data.py; every printed part as STL with features. Not a conventional CAD document.
open_notes.fw: Plan only: reuses Duke V2's deploy code and BHL's policy runner; not written.
open_notes.policy: Stands and crouches under stiff PD in MuJoCo; no walking policy yet.
open_notes.built: Nothing printed or assembled. v0.3 is the first joint-kit test.

robots.summary: Duke Humanoid V2's joint layout on RobStride actuators with every structural part printed, in the spirit of Berkeley Humanoid Lite. A design release: BOM, printable parts, URDF and a MuJoCo standing check exist; nothing has been built.
robots.verdict: Open by construction, unproven by construction. Treat every number as a design estimate until the joint-kit test.

robots.name: Berkeley Humanoid Lite
robots.actuators: 22 printed cycloidal actuators (BLDC motor + custom controller board); the paper abstract states only the sub-$5,000 cost
robots.structure: FDM-printed PLA/PETG structure and gearboxes; off-the-shelf metal parts
robots.price_note: "Sub-$5,000" per the project; itemised Google Sheet BOM linked from the docs.
robots.license_hw: CC BY-SA 4.0 (repository README); MakerWorld files CC BY; the assets repository's LICENCE file

open_notes.cad: Public Onshape document; anonymous export allowed. MakerWorld 3MF print plates.
open_notes.elec: Motor controller firmware is released; the board's design files were not found in the repository.
open_notes.policy: Trained checkpoints ship in the repository; zero-shot sim-to-real walking shown in the paper.
open_notes.built: Built and walking at Berkeley; third-party builds are reported informally, no kit.

robots.summary: The reference for a desktop-printable full-body humanoid: 22 DOF, printed cycloidal gearboxes, everything on hobby-grade tooling, documented failure modes.
robots.verdict: Meets the open-hardware definition and is reproducible on a desktop printer. The first project to study for a low-cost full-body build.

robots.name: Duke Humanoid V2
robots.actuators: RobStride RS00 ×2, RS02 ×6, RS03 ×11, RS04 ×2, RS05 ×6, RS06 ×4; 2 Feetech gripper servos
robots.structure: Machined aluminium 6061; PLA, TPU and SLS nylon-12 prints
robots.price_note: Team BOM grand total $14,882 (CNC parts $6,390). The curated CSVs on the project's hardware site total about $13,000 without consumables.
robots.license_hw: Apache-2.0 (public repository licence, checked 2026-09-25; the docs' licence page says the same for CAD, drawings and BOM)

open_notes.cad: Fusion 360 source, per-part STEP, module tree and drawings.
open_notes.elec: All boards off the shelf: CANable adapters, buck converters, TVS diodes.
open_notes.policy: Deploy code and Isaac Lab training are released; a public walking checkpoint for V2 was not confirmed.
open_notes.lic: The public repository is Apache-2.0 and the documentation applies it to CAD, drawings and BOM. An internal hand-off note in the working copy still calls the decision pending, so confirm the LICENSE file shipped with the CAD release.
open_notes.built: Built and walking at Duke (V2 paper, 2026). V1 (2024) was MIT-licensed.

robots.summary: A 1.26 m, 31-joint RobStride humanoid with two gimballed depth cameras, machined aluminium legs and a fully priced BOM. The design this site's own robot derives from.
robots.verdict: Complete release with real build data under Apache-2.0. The machined parts are the cost and the sourcing burden.

robots.name: Roboto Origin
robots.actuators: 21 servo actuators, 120 N·m legs and 27 N·m arms; models not confirmed
robots.structure: Machined and printed parts; ordered through Taobao and JLC per the project
robots.price_note: About ¥50,000 (≈ $7,000) reported by the project and press; kit pre-orders taken.
robots.license_hw: CERN-OHL-W-2.0 (hardware, PCB, BOM, URDF); CC BY-SA 4.0 (docs)

open_notes.cad: Native SolidWorks parts and assemblies plus manufacturing drawings.
open_notes.elec: Gerbers and schematics; V2 integrates the boards into one core PCB.
open_notes.built: Built, walking and jumping; ~100 kit pre-orders reported. Builders must match mechanical, PCB and firmware revisions.

robots.summary: A 1.25 m full-stack release: native CAD, drawings, PCB source, firmware, URDF/MJCF, ROS 2 deployment and Isaac Lab training, all licensed.
robots.verdict: The strongest large full-stack release found. Needs CNC work and Chinese sourcing; freeze matching revisions before ordering.

robots.name: Asimov v1
robots.actuators: Not stated publicly (25 powered joints + 2 passive toes)
robots.structure: Machined 7075 aluminium and 316L parts, MJF/SLM prints
robots.price_note: DIY kit target ≈ $15,000 with a $499 deposit (summer 2026); an unassembled kit at $20,000 was also reported. BOM by request.

open_notes.cad: 165 per-part STEP files and a whole-robot STEP; no native parametric source.
open_notes.elec: Native KiCad projects with LCSC part numbers.
open_notes.fw: Listed as "coming soon"; the locomotion policy ships inside it.
open_notes.built: Physical prototypes exist; kits not yet delivered.

robots.summary: A 1.2 m, 35 kg humanoid released under CERN-OHL-S with STEP files, KiCad electronics and a MuJoCo model; BOM and firmware still gated.
robots.verdict: An open-licensed release in progress: describe it as it exists, not as the finished platform.

robots.name: Poppy Humanoid
robots.price_note: $8,000–9,000 per the project (2015 pricing, about 60 % actuators).

open_notes.cad: SolidWorks source plus STEP, Parasolid and STL.
open_notes.policy: Walks only with support; not a locomotion platform.
open_notes.built: Many copies built in labs and schools; last hardware release 2015.

robots.summary: The clearest early example of a full robot released as editable CAD rather than printable meshes. Dated actuators and no walking.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition; conceptually sound, technically old.

robots.name: NICO
robots.price_note: No published total.
robots.license_hw: CC BY-SA 3.0 (stated by the project; the CAD repository carries no licence file)

open_notes.cad: Native Autodesk Inventor parts and assemblies plus STLs.
open_notes.policy: Interaction and manipulation platform; it does not walk.
open_notes.built: Several copies in use at Hamburg and partner labs.

robots.summary: A child-sized interaction and manipulation humanoid with genuinely open, creator-owned CAD; dependent on proprietary servos and hands.
robots.verdict: Open where the creators control the design; reproducibility limited by third-party parts and an older software stack.

robots.name: AI Sapiens K0 / K1
robots.price_note: Not announced; Korean press reports under $10,000.
robots.license_hw: Not stated (release announced as open: BOM, CAD, sim assets)

open_notes.cad: Announced as open; files not located at the time of writing.
open_notes.built: Sold and demonstrated by ROBOTIS.

robots.summary: ROBOTIS's 1.3 m humanoid on its Dynamixel Q actuators, announced as an open platform with ROS 2 packages public first.
robots.verdict: Watch: the software is out under Apache-2.0; the hardware release and its licence were not verifiable.

robots.name: K-Bot
robots.actuators: RobStride RS04 ×4, RS03 ×8, RS02 ×6, RS00 ×2 (5 per leg, 5 per arm)
robots.price_note: Pre-order price for the first 100 units; the company closed in November 2025 and refunded orders.
robots.license_sw: GPL-3.0 per README; MIT in the root licence and sub-repositories

open_notes.cad: Onshape and STEP.
open_notes.built: Two units shipped before closure; no complete build path survives.

robots.summary: A 1.4 m open-licensed humanoid whose company dissolved; the CAD and OS remain as a design archive.
robots.verdict: Not reproducible today. The licence preserved the files, not the suppliers or the documentation work.

robots.name: LeRobot Humanoid (biped)
robots.structure: 3D-printed (75 STL parts) with off-the-shelf bearings and fasteners
robots.price_note: ≈ $2,636 as of April 2026 per the hardware repository (motors ≈ $1,880).

open_notes.cad: Public Onshape document organised by subassembly. The model repository's bipedal-platform URDF already carries a folded upper body with RobStride O0 arms, so the upper body exists in CAD; the hardware release covers the biped.
open_notes.policy: MuJoCo and MJLab training environments; walking shown by the authors.
open_notes.built: Lower body only; upper body on the roadmap. Third-party builds not confirmed.

robots.summary: A printed 12-DOF biped on RobStride O-series actuators with an itemised $2,600 BOM, Onshape source and Apache-2.0 terms.
robots.verdict: Incomplete as a humanoid, excellent as a biped: the best-documented low-cost legs in this list.

robots.name: AGILOped
robots.price_note: No procurement BOM.

open_notes.cad: STEP files, URDF and MuJoCo assets.
open_notes.policy: Walking, jumping, fall mitigation and recovery demonstrated.
open_notes.built: Authors only.

robots.summary: A 1.1 m, 14.5 kg walker with strong physical demonstrations and MIT-licensed STEP, but no BOM or assembly manual.
robots.verdict: Incomplete: a model release, not a build release.

robots.name: NimbRo-OP2X
robots.price_note: "Similar price range to Baxter" per the paper; no figure.
robots.license_hw: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (stated in the hardware repository; no licence file)

open_notes.lic: Non-commercial clause fails the open-hardware definition.
open_notes.policy: RoboCup AdultSize champion; walking and perception stack released.

robots.summary: An adult-sized SLS-printed soccer humanoid on Dynamixel XH540s with a released CAD and BOM.
robots.verdict: Reproducible and proven, but non-commercial.

robots.name: igus Humanoid Open Platform
robots.org: University of Bonn, NimbRo with igus
robots.price_note: Printed-parts set priced on request from igus.
robots.license_hw: Not stated on the project page

open_notes.cad: CAD and initial software on GitHub (igusGmbH/HumanoidOpenPlatform).
open_notes.built: RoboCup TeenSize winner 2016; superseded by NimbRo-OP2X.

robots.summary: The 2015 child-sized printed platform that led to NimbRo-OP2X.
robots.verdict: Historical; licence not stated.

robots.name: ToddlerBot 2.0
robots.price_note: ≈ $6,000 BOM per the paper, 90 % in the Jetson and the Dynamixels; a third-party assembled kit is sold at $4,299.

open_notes.docs: MakerWorld 3MF plates with materials and times; JLCPCB ordering walkthrough.
open_notes.lic: Non-commercial terms; a company gets no right to build on the hardware.
open_notes.built: Independent reproductions reported; assembled units sold by a third party.

robots.summary: A 56 cm, 30-DOF, entirely printed humanoid for loco-manipulation learning; the most complete build documentation in the list.
robots.verdict: Excellent source-available research platform; fails the open-hardware definition on the non-commercial clause.

robots.name: Microban
robots.price_note: ≈ $567 in parts before tools, per the project BOM.
robots.summary: A 30 cm, 19-DOF desktop humanoid with a detailed BOM and an RL environment.
robots.verdict: Research-only terms, like ToddlerBot.

robots.name: Zeroth-01 / Z-Bot
robots.compute: Milk-V Duo S (RISC-V) in the original; community builds use a Raspberry Pi 4
robots.price_note: "BoM starts at $350" per the repository.

open_notes.built: Built at hackathons; replaced by Z-Bot, then orphaned when K-Scale closed.

robots.summary: A $350, 16-DOF printed mini humanoid with vision and speech on a RISC-V board.
robots.verdict: Cheap, MIT-licensed, unmaintained.

robots.name: Open Duck Mini v2
robots.actuators: 14 × Feetech STS3215 (5 per leg, 4 in the neck and head)
robots.price_note: "Under $400" per the project; itemised Google Sheet BOM.

open_notes.policy: Trained ONNX walking policies run on the Pi; MuJoCo Playground environment.
open_notes.built: Widely reproduced; third-party kits exist.

robots.summary: A 42 cm walking droid built by hundreds of people for under $400, with the whole RL pipeline public.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition and is reproduced at scale; a biped, not a humanoid.

robots.name: Bolt
robots.org: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative (MPI-IS, NYU, LAAS)
robots.actuators: ODRI brushless modules (T-motor + 9:1 belt stage + open driver board)
robots.compute: Off-board PC via ODRI master board
robots.price_note: ≈ $6,400 to build in the US, estimated by a third party; ODRI publishes the BOM.

open_notes.elec: Driver and master boards are open designs.
open_notes.built: Reproduced in several labs.

robots.summary: A 6-DOF research biped built from ODRI's open actuator module and electronics.
robots.verdict: Fully open and reproduced; a lab platform rather than a humanoid.

robots.name: MEVITA
robots.actuators: CubeMars AK70-10 and AK10-9 V2 (MIT mode)
robots.price_note: No published total.

open_notes.cad: CAD on Google Drive.

robots.summary: A minimal sheet-metal biped on CubeMars actuators with the full sim-to-real pipeline released.
robots.verdict: Open and clever; no BOM total.

robots.name: HopeJR
robots.org: The Robot Studio with Hugging Face
robots.actuators: Feetech STS-series bus servos (arms and hands)
robots.price_note: ≈ $3,000 per Hugging Face's announcement; no whole-robot BOM.
robots.license_hw: Apache-2.0 on the Humanoid subtree; root and newer arm subtree unlicensed

open_notes.built: Arms and hands demonstrated with glove teleoperation; no walking controller.

robots.summary: Printed arms and dexterous hands on bus servos, teleoperated with gloves; a full-body concept with the upper body real.
robots.verdict: Incomplete and inconsistently licensed across the repository.

robots.name: Amazing Hand
robots.price_note: Under €200 per hand in off-the-shelf parts per Pollen's BOM.

open_notes.built: Reproduced widely since release.

robots.summary: An 8-DOF printed hand for under €200 with BOM, print guide and assembly guide.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition; the cheapest open hand worth bolting on.

robots.name: InMoov
robots.price_note: $1,000–1,500 per builders' reports; parts list on the project site.

open_notes.cad: STL only.
open_notes.built: Thousands built; legs are not motorised.

robots.summary: The original life-size printable maker humanoid: upper body, hobby servos, huge community.
robots.verdict: A maker platform under non-commercial terms, not a walking robot.

robots.name: ROBOTIS OP3
robots.price_note: List price at ROBOTIS US.
robots.license_hw: STP parts and schematics published; no unified hardware licence (Dynamixel firmware closed)

open_notes.cad: STP exports of every frame.
open_notes.elec: OpenCR board is open (BOM, Gerbers, firmware); the actuators are not.

robots.summary: A supported commercial kid-size humanoid with unusually complete public drawings and ROS software.
robots.verdict: Inspectable and modifiable, not open all the way down.

robots.name: iCub
robots.actuators: Custom brushless and brushed motors with in-house boards
robots.price_note: Supplied by IIT; about €250,000 per unit is the commonly cited figure (Wikipedia), depending on version.
robots.license_hw: CERN-OHL-W-2.0 for the public subset; CC BY-SA models; historically GPL/LGPL

open_notes.cad: Public repositories mirror selected material from private engineering repositories.
open_notes.built: Dozens of units in labs worldwide.

robots.summary: The long-running open research humanoid: open software and models, selected open hardware, commercial supply.
robots.verdict: Calling it closed would be wrong; calling every part open hardware would also be wrong.

robots.name: BRUCE
robots.price_note: Limited-time price; list price $15,290.
robots.license_hw: GPL-3.0 with a commercial licence option

open_notes.cad: Wiki and CAD behind developer access at the time of writing.

robots.summary: A kid-size compliant biped sold as an open platform on proprietary BEAR actuators.
robots.verdict: Open-source software, gated hardware.

robots.name: AgiBot X1 (Lingxi X1)
robots.price_note: Kits listed by resellers; no project BOM total.

open_notes.cad: Native SolidWorks archives, whole-machine STEP, drawings and assembly SOP.
open_notes.lic: The hardware repository has no licence granting reuse.

robots.summary: A 1.3 m modular humanoid with native CAD, BOM and SOP published, but no hardware licence.
robots.verdict: Files without permission: fails the definition on licensing alone.

robots.name: Fourier N1
robots.price_note: Not published.

open_notes.cad: Announced as fully open with BOM, STEP and SOP; the public repository is SDK documentation only.

robots.summary: Announced as the first open-source humanoid; the hardware package had not appeared where the announcement pointed.
robots.verdict: Promised, not delivered.

robots.name: Tien Kung (Tiangong)
robots.org: X-Humanoid, Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center
robots.price_note: Not published.

open_notes.cad: URDF and STL released; hardware design release announced for Tien Kung 3.0, not found.

robots.summary: A full-size running humanoid with open training code and URDF; hardware openness announced repeatedly.
robots.verdict: Open software around closed hardware until the CAD appears.

robots.name: OpenLoong
robots.price_note: Not published.

open_notes.cad: STEP exports and PDFs; no native CAD, ECAD or full arm and hand source.

robots.summary: A licensed but thin hardware tree: STEP and PDFs without BOM.
robots.verdict: Licence ahead of reproducibility.

robots.name: XLeRobot
robots.actuators: Feetech STS3215 bus servos: two SO-101 arms (6 each, gripper included), 2-DOF head, LeKiwi three-wheel omni base
robots.structure: 3D-printed parts on an IKEA cart with a LeKiwi base
robots.compute: Your laptop, or a Raspberry Pi (+$79)
robots.price_note: $660 base configuration per the project; RGB cameras +$30, Raspberry Pi +$79, RealSense +$220.

open_notes.docs: Assembly under four hours per the project; tutorial videos.
open_notes.policy: VLA and RL training code and a MuJoCo environment; no single released household policy.
open_notes.built: Thousands of builders; kits sold by several vendors.

robots.summary: Two SO-101 arms and a head on a LeKiwi omni base and an IKEA cart: a $660 dual-arm mobile home robot on the LeRobot stack.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition and is the most reproduced bimanual mobile platform in the list.

robots.name: LeKiwi
robots.actuators: Feetech STS3215: SO-101 arm (6 incl. gripper) and three base wheels
robots.price_note: $482 for the 12 V build, $499 for 5 V, $184 wired, per the project's BOM (US prices).

open_notes.built: Kits sold by ROBOTIS America and others; widely built.

robots.summary: A holonomic three-wheel base that carries an SO-101 arm and a Raspberry Pi for under $500, on the LeRobot stack.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition; the base under XLeRobot.

robots.name: SO-ARM101
robots.org: The Robot Studio with Hugging Face
robots.actuators: 6 × Feetech STS3215 (7.4 V), 5 joints plus gripper
robots.compute: Host PC over a serial bus adapter
robots.price_note: ≈ $122 for a follower arm, ≈ $230 for a leader-follower pair, per the repository.

open_notes.cad: STEP and STL.
open_notes.built: Around ten kit vendors on three continents; the default LeRobot arm.

robots.summary: The $120 printed 6-DOF arm that most LeRobot demos run on; STEP, BOM, guide and many vendors.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition and is reproduced at scale.

robots.name: OpenArm v1
robots.actuators: Damiao DM-J4310 and DM-8009P quasi-direct-drive motors on CAN, 7 per arm plus grippers
robots.structure: Machined aluminium and sheet metal; 606 mm reach, 6 kg peak payload per arm
robots.price_note: ≈ $6,500 for a complete bimanual system from the licensed vendors.

open_notes.cad: STEP per part (v1.0), whole-arm STEP and BOM for later versions; SolidWorks since 2025-08.
open_notes.bom: Machined parts carry MISUMI meviy part numbers so they can be ordered without CAD.
open_notes.policy: Force-feedback teleoperation and ROS 2 control; no released manipulation policy.

robots.summary: A 7-DOF-per-arm bimanual system on Damiao QDD motors with strong CAD, BOM and ROS 2 support.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition; the reference for a torque-controlled open arm.

robots.name: Mobile ALOHA
robots.actuators: Two Trossen ViperX 300 arms (Dynamixel) on an AgileX Tracer base, plus two leader arms
robots.structure: Aluminium extrusion frame on a commercial base
robots.price_note: Under $32,000 including power and compute per the paper; the stationary ALOHA is about $20,000.
robots.license_hw: Not stated for the hardware (CAD and BOM public); MIT code

open_notes.lic: The hardware tutorial publishes CAD and BOM without a stated licence; code is MIT.
open_notes.policy: ACT training code and pre-trained models.
open_notes.built: Reproduced in many labs; Trossen sells kits.

robots.summary: The bimanual teleoperation cart that started the low-cost imitation-learning wave: two ViperX arms, a Tracer base, ACT.
robots.verdict: Reproducible and widely reproduced; the hardware licence is unstated.

robots.name: TidyBot++
robots.actuators: Four powered casters (holonomic base); carries any arm (Kinova, Franka, ARX5, xArm, UR5, ViperX shown)
robots.price_note: $5,000–6,000 to fabricate the base per the authors; arm not included.

open_notes.policy: Diffusion policies trained on its phone-teleop data are demonstrated.
open_notes.built: Built at Stanford and Princeton; third-party builds not confirmed.

robots.summary: An open holonomic base with powered casters for any arm, with CAD, BOM and a build guide.
robots.verdict: Meets the definition; a base, not a complete robot.

robots.name: Solo 12
robots.org: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative (MPI-IS, NYU, LAAS)
robots.actuators: 12 ODRI brushless modules (T-motor + 9:1 belt stage + open driver board)
robots.compute: Off-board PC via the ODRI master board
robots.price_note: Solo 8 at about €4,000 in components per ODRI; Solo 12 sold as a kit or assembled by PAL Robotics.

open_notes.built: Reproduced in many labs; kits from PAL.

robots.summary: The 2.5 kg, 12-DOF open quadruped built from ODRI's actuator module; the same module as Bolt.
robots.verdict: Fully open and reproduced; the reference legged platform.

robots.name: YOR
robots.actuators: Two compliant arms with grippers on a telescopic lift and an omnidirectional base (models in the paper)
robots.price_note: $9,250 BOM per the paper.

open_notes.built: Authors' units only at the time of writing.

robots.summary: A sub-$10k bimanual mobile manipulator with a vertical lift, released with off-the-shelf CAD and BOM.
robots.verdict: Open and inexpensive; new, so not yet reproduced.
